question: What is the minimum age to qualify for an Ohio real estate broker's license?
explanation: ORC 4735.07 sets the broker applicant minimum age at 18 -- notably the SAME minimum used for an Ohio salesperson license, unlike many states that set a higher minimum age (often 21) for a broker's license than for a salesperson's license.

question: Ohio's 18-year-old minimum age for a broker's license is notable because it:
choice_a: Is three years higher than the salesperson minimum
choice_b: Is identical to the state's minimum age for a salesperson's license
choice_c: Applies only to applicants who were never previously licensed as a salesperson
choice_d: Was raised to 21 for all applicants after 2001
explanation: Unlike states that impose a separate, higher age floor for broker licensure, ORC 4735.07 uses the same 18-year-old minimum for both salesperson and broker applicants.

question: Under ORC 4735.07, how much recent licensed experience must a broker applicant have?
choice_a: Licensed as a salesperson for at least five consecutive years immediately before applying
choice_b: Licensed as a broker in another state for at least one year
choice_c: Licensed as a real estate broker or salesperson for at least two of the preceding five years
choice_d: No prior licensure is required if the applicant holds a bachelor's degree
explanation: ORC 4735.07 requires the applicant to have been a licensed real estate broker or salesperson for at least two of the five years preceding the application -- either license type counts toward this experience requirement.

question: Besides the two-of-five-years licensure requirement, what transaction-based experience must a broker applicant show under ORC 4735.07?
choice_a: Completion of at least 50 real estate sales transactions with no substitute allowed
choice_b: Personal ownership of at least two investment properties
choice_c: Supervision of at least one licensed salesperson for a full year
choice_d: Completion of at least 20 real estate sales transactions in that period, or equivalent experience under Commission rule
explanation: ORC 4735.07 requires the applicant to have completed at least 20 real estate sales transactions (acting as broker or salesperson) during the qualifying period, or to show equivalent experience as defined by Commission rule.

question: Can an Ohio broker applicant satisfy the 20-transaction requirement of ORC 4735.07 without having personally closed 20 sales?
choice_a: Yes -- the Real Estate Commission may recognize equivalent experience by rule in place of the 20-transaction count
choice_b: No -- 20 completed sales transactions is an absolute, non-waivable minimum
choice_c: Yes, but only by paying an additional experience-waiver fee
choice_d: No -- the requirement can only be met through salesperson-side transactions, never broker-side
explanation: ORC 4735.07 allows the 20-transaction benchmark to be satisfied through equivalent experience recognized under a rule adopted by the Ohio Real Estate Commission, giving the Commission flexibility for non-traditional experience paths.

question: For a broker applicant licensed as a salesperson on or after August 1, 2001, how many hours of pre-license instruction in real estate PRACTICE does ORC 4735.07 require?
explanation: ORC 4735.07(B)(6)(b) requires 40 hours of instruction in real estate practice as part of the broker pre-licensure curriculum for applicants licensed as a salesperson on or after 8/1/2001.

question: How many hours of instruction in Ohio real estate law and civil rights law (municipal, state, and federal) does ORC 4735.07(B)(6)(b) require of a broker applicant?
explanation: ORC 4735.07(B)(6)(b) requires 40 hours of instruction covering Ohio real estate law together with municipal, state, and federal civil rights law -- the same 40-hour figure as the real estate practice requirement.

question: How many hours of pre-license instruction in real estate APPRAISAL does ORC 4735.07(B)(6)(b) require of a broker applicant?
explanation: ORC 4735.07(B)(6)(b) requires 20 hours of instruction in real estate appraisal, the same figure required for real estate finance.

question: How many hours of pre-license instruction in real estate FINANCE does ORC 4735.07(B)(6)(b) require of a broker applicant?
explanation: ORC 4735.07(B)(6)(b) requires 20 hours of instruction in real estate finance, matching the 20-hour appraisal requirement.

question: Beyond practice, law/civil rights, appraisal, and finance, ORC 4735.07(B)(6)(b) also requires broker applicants to complete instruction in financial management, human resource/personnel management, applied business economics, and business law. How many hours does each of these four subjects require?
explanation: ORC 4735.07(B)(6)(b) requires 30 hours of instruction in each of financial management, human resource/personnel management, applied business economics, and business law -- four additional subjects beyond the core practice/law/appraisal/finance curriculum.

question: Adding up all eight subject areas ORC 4735.07(B)(6)(b) requires for a post-8/1/2001-licensed broker applicant (40 + 40 + 20 + 20 practice/law/appraisal/finance hours, plus 30 hours each in financial management, HR/personnel management, applied business economics, and business law), what is the total pre-license education requirement?
explanation: 40 + 40 + 20 + 20 = 120 hours in the four core subjects, plus 30 hours x 4 additional subjects = 120 more hours, for a combined total of 240 hours of pre-license broker education under ORC 4735.07(B)(6)(b).

question: After receiving an Ohio broker's license, how many hours of post-licensing instruction must a new broker complete, and by when?
choice_a: 20 hours, within 6 months of license issuance
choice_b: 10 hours, within 24 months of license issuance
choice_c: 30 hours, within 12 months of license issuance
choice_d: 10 hours, within 12 months of license issuance
explanation: ORC 4735.07 requires a new broker to submit proof of completing 10 hours of post-licensing instruction, approved by the Commission, within 12 months of license issuance -- separate from the continuing education a broker must complete to renew.

question: Under ORC 4735.08, what score-related condition must be satisfied before the superintendent may issue a broker's license?
choice_a: The applicant must have passed the required licensing examination
choice_b: The applicant's exam score must be published in the county recorder's office
choice_c: The applicant must retake the exam annually for the first three years
choice_d: No exam is required if the applicant already held a salesperson license for 10+ years
explanation: ORC 4735.08 sets out conditions the superintendent must confirm before issuing a broker's license, including that the applicant has passed the required examination.

question: If a real estate brokerage applying for licensure is organized as a PARTNERSHIP, what does ORC 4735.08 require of its officers or partners?
choice_a: Only the managing partner needs to hold a broker's license
choice_b: Each partner or officer of the partnership must themselves be a licensed real estate broker
choice_c: Partners are exempt from individual licensure if the partnership itself is licensed
choice_d: At least one partner must hold a salesperson's license, but a broker's license is not required
explanation: ORC 4735.08 conditions license issuance to a partnership on every officer or partner of that partnership being individually licensed as a real estate broker.

question: What process does ORC 4735.06 govern with respect to becoming a licensed Ohio real estate broker?
choice_a: The renewal cycle for an existing broker's license
choice_b: The disciplinary hearing process for license revocation
choice_c: The filing of an application for a broker's license
choice_d: The formation requirements for a real estate limited liability company
explanation: ORC 4735.06 governs the broker license application itself -- distinct from 4735.07's substantive qualification requirements and 4735.08's conditions for actually issuing the license.
source_note: hedge: ORC 4735.06 is confirmed as the broker application section by title/subject, but this project's research pass did not independently pull its full procedural text (e.g., specific form or fee details), so the question is limited to the section's general subject matter.

question: In Ohio, is a "principal broker" a separate license category from an ordinary real estate broker?
choice_a: Yes -- principal brokers must pass a distinct principal-broker licensing exam
choice_b: Yes -- principal brokers are licensed under a different chapter of the Revised Code than other brokers
choice_c: No -- but only salespersons, not brokers, may be designated principal broker
choice_d: No -- principal broker is a designation held by a licensed broker within a brokerage, not a separate license type
explanation: ORC 4735.081 requires every brokerage to designate one of its licensed brokers as "principal broker." This is a role/designation assigned to someone who already holds the standard broker's license under 4735.07-.08, not a separate license tier or a separate exam.

question: Does the broker's licensing examination differ depending on whether a person will later be designated their brokerage's principal broker?
choice_a: No -- the same broker examination and licensure requirements under ORC 4735.07-.08 apply regardless of a later principal-broker designation
choice_b: Yes -- a supplemental principal-broker exam module is required before the designation is valid
choice_c: Yes -- principal brokers must pass the exam with a higher minimum score than other brokers
choice_d: No -- but principal brokers must complete an additional 240 hours of pre-license education beyond ORC 4735.07
explanation: Because "principal broker" is a designation under ORC 4735.081 rather than a distinct license class, the underlying broker qualification exam and pre-license education requirements of ORC 4735.07-.08 are identical whether or not that broker is later designated principal broker of a brokerage.
